objective: Managing requirement changes by assessing impact, dependencies, and risk against the change-control plan and requirements baseline
secondaryObjectives: Communicating requirements status to the project manager and stakeholders: issues, conflicts, changes, risks, and overall status
Tracking requirements using traceability artifacts/tools to provide evidence of delivery against what was stated

sources.cite: PMI, Professional in Business Analysis (PMI-PBA) exam: Needs Assessment 18%, Planning 22%, Analysis 35%, Traceability and Monitoring 15%, Evaluation 10%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through summarizing fetches of two study pages: examcert.app (2026-08-16), which says its weights 'come from the current PMI exam outline', and masteryexamprep's PMI-PBA syllabus, which cites the PMI-PBA Handbook (revised 24 May 2022) and quotes tasks such as 'Initiate and document requirement changes using agreed change control processes and tooling' and 'Identify acceptance responsibilities (who accepts, evidence required, sign-off process) and align stakeholders'. Neither page quotes PMI's task statements on the requirements baseline; PMI's outline PDF was not opened. The objective wording is the course seed's, to verify. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's pmipba-claims-portal-baseline-signoff (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the business analyst for a fictional council's planning-permission portal. The requirements baseline was signed off; build is half done. The planning director asks for an urgent change.
handover: Traceability matrix links 64 requirements to designs and test cases.
Change control: impact analysis, then the change board.
howItWorks: The dashboard shows the commitments, the work items, the risks and issues, the people's support and the milestones.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each status meeting; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Week 2: the 3D upload breaks the document store's retention rule; the release fails its records audit.
Week 3: the release date is announced; the four blocked requirements surface in testing and the date slips.
Week 4: after release, screen-reader users can't use the fee calculator; a complaint goes to the council.

chgPrompt.context: The planning director wants 3D model uploads in this release.

choices.label: Trace its impact (9 requirements, storage, tests, retention, 3 weeks, 40 thousand dollars), assess the risk, and take it to the change board with options

effects.log: The board defers it to release 2 with the impact on record.

choices.feedback: Changes to a baselined set go through impact analysis and change control.

choices.label: Add a simplified version without the board
choices.feedback: Even a small change to the baseline needs control and traced impact.

choices.feedback: Untraced, the change breaks dependent requirements and the retention rule.

statPrompt.title: Reporting status
statPrompt.context: Four requirements are blocked by a design conflict.

choices.label: Report status by requirement state, the four blocked by the conflict with options, the deferred change, and the risks, to the PM and stakeholders

choices.label: Report '60 of 64 on track'
choices.feedback: The four blocked ones are the important part.

choices.label: Leave the conflict out until it's solved
choices.feedback: The PM plans the release without knowing four requirements are blocked.

scoring.modelReasoning: Once requirements are baselined, changes are traced for impact on dependent requirements, design, tests and rules, and decided through change control. Requirements status reports states, conflicts, changes and risks. Traceability links each requirement to tests, so delivery is evidenced rather than assumed.
